pull.title: KAFKA-21344: Handle partition rotation for share fetches
pull.body:
A share fetch hands its record budget to partitions in the order they
are read, so the partition read first  takes the largest share. Two
things decided that order earlier and together they could starve a
partition, hence changed the behaviour.

Earlier:
- `SharePartitionManager` rotated the fetch list by `sessionEpoch %
size`. The client bumps the epoch on both
  ShareFetch and ShareAcknowledge, so in a poll-and-commit loop fetch
epochs step by two and the rotation is
  constant. One unpaired request flips the parity, and with two
partitions the rotation then undoes the
  session reorder on every fetch, so the same partition is read first
until the other starves.
- `ShareSessionContext` moved served partitions to the end of the
session from inside the response iterator,
  in the iteration order of the response map. That map had passed
through `HashMap` copies, so when every
  partition returned records the session ended up in hash order and the
same partition led every fetch.

PR:

This change removes the epoch rotation from the fetch path and makes the
session reorder deterministic from  the fetch order. The fetch order is
preserved through `ShareFetchUtils`, `ShareFetch` and `KafkaApis` with
`LinkedHashMap`s. `ShareSessionContext` reorders the session in one pass
before pruning the response:  partitions without records keep their
position at the front, and partitions with records are appended in fetch
order rotated by one, so the partition read first is read last next
time. `PartitionRotateStrategy`  is reduced to that rotation and the
unused `sessionEpoch` parameter of `fetchMessages` is dropped.

`ShareConsumerFairnessTest` adds cases for the epoch parity change, for
the first position rotating when all partitions return records with
explicit and implicit acknowledgement, and for an idle partition being
read first once it has records.

`SharePartitionManagerTest` verifies the session order across subsequent
fetches.

Reviewers: Abhinav Dixit <adixit@confluent.io>, Andrew Schofield
 <aschofield@confluent.io>

reviews.body:
Thanks for the PR.

One other question. In DelayedShareFetch when combining newly read and already fetched partitions, can the order of the combination adversely affect the fairness?
Overall LGTM. Just 1 scenario pointed where a starvation could occur. The case pointed out can be solved with lag aware assignor though and it isn't exactly starvation
Looks good to me. Thanks for the valuable improvement.

review_comments.body: We are almost consistent with the use of `LinkedHashMap` across all code paths, but this one is an outlier.

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -215,6 +212,42 @@ public ShareFetchResponse updateAndGenerateResponseData(String groupId, String m } } + /** + * Re-orders the partitions of the session as per the records returned in the response. The subsequent + * fetch reads the partitions in the order of the session, hence the partitions which returned records + * are moved to the end so the partitions which did not return records are read first. Among the partitions + * which returned records, the partition read first takes the largest share of the records, hence they are + * appended in the order decided by the {@link PartitionRotateStrategy} so the first position rotates. + *

+ * The updates are expected in the fetch order of the partitions. + * + * @param updates The response data for the partitions, in fetch order. + */ + private void updatePartitionOrder(LinkedHashMap updates) {
review_comments.body: `updatePartitionOrder` keeps unserved partitions at the front and rotates only the served block left by one, so in the bands where exactly one partition goes unserved (or n is odd and two are served) the session locks into a fixed cycle in which the middle partitions keep their slots and one partition only ever receives the leftover record budget.

issue_comments.body:
> Thanks for the PR.
> 
> One other question. In DelayedShareFetch when combining newly read and already fetched partitions, can the order of the combination adversely affect the fairness?

The problem is that for shared partitions you can never guarantee that which partitions attain fetch locks across different clients, when multiple same set of partitions are requested concurrently by different client hence fetch lock acquisition will play a role as well. But the partitions fetch strategy now prioritizes the partitions which went unserved. So I don't think eventually `combine` method will make a difference.

commit.message: KAFKA-21344: Handle partition rotation for share fetches
Drop unused epoch parameter and assert fetch order in tests
Produce only the records the rotation fairness tests consume
